name: Cathedral of St. John the Baptist
history: Savannah's Catholics built a small frame church of St. John the Baptist in 1799. It became the cathedral when the diocese was formed in 1850. The present cathedral's cornerstone was laid in 1873 and it was dedicated in 1876. Spires were added in 1896; fire gutted the interior in 1898, and it was rebuilt and consecrated in 1920. It became a basilica in 2020.
arch: French Gothic Revival by Ephraim Francis Baldwin, stuccoed and whitewashed, with twin spires near Lafayette Square.
features: Its stained glass windows were installed in 1904, made in Austria-Hungary.
The cathedral was briefly named Our Lady of Perpetual Help before reverting to St. John the Baptist in 1883.

look.d: The spires, added in 1896, are a Savannah skyline landmark.
The windows came from Austria-Hungary in 1904.

fun: It was rebuilt after the 1898 fire, but took 13 more years to fully finish.
journal: Twin white spires above Savannah's squares and live oaks. Rebuilt after fire.

quiz.q: When did it become a basilica?
